title: Evaluation of the Ergonomics and Usability of a Point-of-Care Handheld Ultrasound System Using Mixed Reality (MR) Glasses
summary:
Background:
Ultrasound-guided vascular access is an established procedure in emergency and critical care medicine. However, when using conventional ultrasound systems, clinicians often have to shift their gaze between the puncture site and the monitor, which impairs hand-eye coordination and potentially compromises safety. New technologies such as virtual reality (VR) goggles make it possible to display the ultrasound image directly in the field of view and could thus facilitate the procedure.

Research Question:
The aim of the study is to investigate whether the use of VR goggles during ultrasound-guided punctures improves user-friendliness, ergonomics, and safety compared to conventional display methods.

Methodology:
The study will be conducted in two phases: First, an investigation will be carried out under standardized conditions using a medical training model (dummy) to assess usability and safety. Subsequently, the method will be applied in routine clinical practice during medically necessary vascular punctures. Assessment will be conducted using standardized questionnaires and structured observation. Additionally, procedural data and potential complications will be recorded.
conditions: Generally speaking, these patients are individuals who are in the intensive care unit (ICU) or intermediate care unit (IMC) due to various medical conditions.
